clue.text: Beginning of spring? That should get you going

definitions.meaning: read literally, the start of a leap or bound
a boost given to a flat car battery or to a stalled project

explanation.surface: A seasonal remark about the first days of spring, then a promise of fresh energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but here it means a leap, so its beginning is the start of that leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost from another battery revives a stalled car, and figuratively any kick that gets something moving again.

clue.text: See 11
A couple of doctors like a port

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is one doctor
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the second doctor
as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: Two doctors share a fondness for a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the drink, but it is a harbour city in Kenya. 'A couple of doctors' gives two abbreviations, MO and MB.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya's main seaport on the Indian Ocean coast is a well-known harbour city.

clue.text: See 24
An old tree full of life originally, an exceptional thing

indicators.note: full of means the tree word contains the extra letter

parts.note: may is the hawthorn tree

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient tree once bursting with life, now a rare oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY is the British name for hawthorn, its blossom out in May.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that deviates from the norm is an oddity, one standing out from the rule.

clue.text: Stick-like and sticky? But the name hasn't stuck!

parts.note: as thin as a stick
gummy means sticky, like gum

explanation.surface: A puzzle about stickiness, ending in a joke about a forgotten name.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sticking: a word used when a name fails to stay in the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder word for something whose proper name one cannot recall, like whatsit or doodah.

clue.text: Cool — nothing to add!

definitions.meaning: a drink served without water or mixer added

explanation.surface: Someone approves an idea and says there is nothing more to contribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang approval, as in 'that's really good', and a spirit served undiluted, straight from the bottle.

clue.text: Love in contrivance of 1 down and a late 23

indicators.note: a contrivance is a devised arrangement, so the love letter goes in among these words and all are reworked

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A love scene concocted from a crossword's own clue references and a dead performer.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' looks like a pointer to the clue at 1 down, but is read literally as a numeral and a word. '23' is the answer to 23 down, an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hollywood film star of West Side Story and Rebel Without a Cause, so a performer.

clue.text: Alliance lamenting jerks

indicators.note: jerks means jolts about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A political pact is mourned by some idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' looks like a noun for fools; it is the verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouping of nations or parties on the same side, as in political or military allegiance.

clue.text: Sack of fruit with old plant

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: A bag of plums described alongside some ancient plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack of fruit' gives the fruit first: a plum bag, and O for old follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadwort, a flowering shrub with pale blue blooms, is the common example of this genus of plants.

clue.text: Arctic resident maintaining temperature — that makes sense

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the Arctic word holds the other letter within it

parts.note: the Inuit are a people of the Arctic

explanation.surface: An Arctic dweller keeping warm, which the speaker finds perfectly reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that makes sense' reads as an idiom of agreement; only 'sense', the verb, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive something by instinct rather than reasoning is to grasp it without being told.

clue.text: Statement by filmed divorcee, retracted

indicators.note: to retract is to draw back, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Kramer vs. Kramer is a 1979 film about a divorcing couple

explanation.surface: A divorced film star makes a public comment and then takes it back.
explanation.walkthrough: Either of the Kramers in the film Kramer vs. Kramer is a divorcee on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A comment or observation someone voices is a statement in the everyday sense.

clue.text: 23 in a short run features in Guardian story

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear inside it, so the middle pieces go into the other pair

parts.note: a guardian angel watches over someone
a story can be a lie, a fib
taken as written

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to jog is to run gently

explanation.surface: A brief jog by a performer is reported in a Guardian newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper; it is a guardian angel. '23' refers to the answer of 23 down, an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar-winning American film performer, so an example of the person who plays roles on screen.

clue.text: Wolves team surrendering lead twice, shooting high

indicators.note: twice says the shortened word is written two times
giving up its lead means losing its first letter

parts.note: a group of wolves hunting together is a pack

explanation.surface: Wolverhampton Wanderers, the football club called Wolves, twice give up the lead in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, but here it is literal: a wolf team is a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Old military slang for anti-aircraft gunfire, aimed up at enemy planes in the sky.

clue.text: Formerly little money in ransom I set, necessary to rise

indicators.note: to rise says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A kidnapper says the ransom figure must go up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to rise' means read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A former coin of Italy worth one hundredth of a lira, a very small sum of money.

clue.text: Toy with lift key here — helium unnecessary for toy operator

indicators.note: to toy with is to play about with, so these letters are played into a new order
unnecessary says the gas symbol is left out of the jumbled letters

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: Instructions for a toy: no helium needed, just lift it up here.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from LIFT KEY HERE and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flies a kite on a string is the operator of that toy.

clue.text: Dear me, my mongrel whined!

indicators.note: a mongrel is a mixed breed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An exasperated owner complains that their mutt has been whimpering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' seems to be the dog that whined; it signals the mixing of DEAR ME MY.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble or complain loudly and persistently, a near synonym of whine.

clue.text: One getting fuel emptied into buttocks, blows up

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: into means the short piece goes inside the word for buttocks

parts.note: nates is the anatomical Latin term for the buttocks

indicators.note: emptied means the word loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A slightly rude picture of someone pumping fuel into a backside until it swells.
explanation.walkthrough: The buttocks word is anatomical Latin, rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Fills with air so as to expand, as a balloon or tyre is pumped up.

clue.text: Rope in ground keeping beam up

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the ground word holds the other piece

parts.note: land is ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A rope on the ground holds up a wooden beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' suggests timber; it is a ray of light, turned round by 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cord or rope, especially one on a ship or worn around the neck to hold something.

clue.text: Contemptuous remarks, as bones turned up in the middle of Portsmouth

indicators.note: in places the turned bones within the central letters
the middle of picks the two central letters of the city name
in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: sacra is the plural of sacrum, the bone at the base of the spine

explanation.surface: Bones dug up in central Portsmouth prompt scornful comments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is only a link here. Portsmouth, an English naval city, has ten letters, so its middle is a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking, cutting irony aimed at belittling someone is a form of scorn.

clue.text: Spirited point in wise broadcast?

indicators.note: in places the compass word inside the other letters
broadcast means the word is heard spoken, and its sound spelled as letters

parts.note: spoken, wise sounds like Y's, two letter Ys
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A lively compass point turns up in a clever radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'wise' is 'Y's', a pair of Ys, which wrap around EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Frothy and fermenting like dough or beer, hence lively and exuberant in manner.

clue.text: See 21
Spillage of onanist on pioneering physician providing parts for 23

indicators.note: on says the scrambled letters come after the first name
parts means splits open, so one word is placed inside the physician's name

parts.note: Edward Jenner pioneered the smallpox vaccine
providing means if, as a condition

indicators.note: a spillage spreads things about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky medical vignette involving a pioneering doctor and a spillage.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' is the answer to 23 down, an actor; the Friends star is one. Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine.
explanation.definitionFit: An American screen star best known for the sitcom Friends, so an example of a performer.

clue.text: Reportedly take offence at description of female in union

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard, spelled differently

parts.note: to bridle at something is to take offence at it

explanation.surface: A woman in a trade union is said to resent how she is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but it is a marriage: the adjective describes the woman being wed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective belongs to a woman being married, as in a bridal gown or bridal party.

clue.text: Stop a couple talking a foreign language

parts.note: to ban something is to stop it

indicators.note: talking says the number is heard, written as it sounds

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: Telling a pair to stop chatting in a strange tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of languages spoken across central and southern Africa, foreign to English speakers.

clue.text: One taking a part, a part that's uninitiated

indicators.note: uninitiated means without its first letter, its initial

parts.note: a factor is a part or component of a whole

explanation.surface: A newcomer takes a role, without any initiation.
explanation.walkthrough: FACTOR, a contributing part, loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer plays a role in a stage play or film, and so takes on a character.

clue.text: 23 has a wrinkly bum

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means poor or faulty, so the letters are in a bad, wrong order

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that some performer has a wrinkled backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the backside being described; it signals the anagram of HAS A WRINKLY. '23' is the answer to 23 down, an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-time Oscar-winning American film star, so an example of a performer.

clue.text: Comment as a huge amount inside volcano backfires

indicators.note: backfires means the whole construction comes out back to front
inside places the amount within the name of the volcano

parts.note: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily
tons, a ton, means a huge amount informally

explanation.surface: A remark about a huge eruption as a volcano blasts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfires' turns round the whole assembled string, not just the volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: To add explanatory notes or remarks to a text, which is to comment on it.

clue.text: See 6 down
Odd bean, say, for bootlegger

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a runner bean is a type of bean, so runner is an example

explanation.surface: A strange bean is held up as an illegal liquor trader.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is British slang for strange; a runner bean is a common British climbing bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler of illicit liquor, especially during Prohibition, is a kind of bootlegger.
